name: Buehler molecular-DFT multi-agent demonstration
demonstrated_target: finite organic molecules CCCCXCC, with X = C, O or N
boundary_conditions: molecular-coordinate DFT calculations; boundary conditions not independently resolved
locator: Section 2.3.1 Molecular Design; Table 8; Materials and Methods
evidence: Planner, coordinate-retriever and execution-capable chatbot agents devise a plan, obtain molecular coordinates from SMILES, call a supplied DFT function for the three molecular variants, analyze computed energies and answer the user.
all_sources: https://pubs.acs.org/doi/abs/10.1021/acsengineeringau.3c00058 [Section 2.3.1 Molecular Design; Table 8; Materials and Methods] | https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.19998 [Submission record, 30 October 2023; abstract]
limitations: Unnamed, small worked demonstration rather than a separately branded general-purpose package. Counting demonstrates agent-run DFT, not scientific validity of ranking absolute energies of molecules with different compositions. The MechGPT/RAG question-answering demonstrations in the same paper are not separately counted.

name: ProtAgents
demonstrated_target: PDB and de novo proteins; coarse-grained protein elastic networks
boundary_conditions: Finite protein structures represented by anisotropic spring networks; no periodic-cell example is inferred
locator: Results §2.1–2.3 and Fig.3; Materials and Methods, Natural vibrational frequency calculations
evidence: GPT-4 agents plan and invoke protein generation/folding and physics calculations; examples execute ProDy anisotropic-network normal-mode calculations on retrieved and generated structures. Chroma and OmegaFold generate the protein geometries.
all_sources: https://arxiv.org/html/2402.04268v1 [Results §2.1–2.3 and Fig.3; Materials and Methods, Natural vibrational frequency calculations] | https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.04268 [Submission history, v1]
limitations: F denotes an actual coarse-grained elastic-network vibration calculation, not quantum-chemical molecular frequencies or ideal-gas thermochemistry. No D mark: MD is mentioned as an extensible capability and used in training another predictor, rather than demonstrated as an agent-run dynamics task.

name: LLaMP
demonstrated_target: Si crystal/interstitial and crystal annealing MD
boundary_conditions: crystalline supercells demonstrated; PBC not separately audited
evidence: Fetches a crystal, constructs a supercell, runs temperature-cycling ML-potential MD and analyzes its trajectory.

name: ChemReasoner
demonstrated_target: heterogeneous catalyst slabs and adsorbates
boundary_conditions: slab cells and vacuum explicitly reported
evidence: LLM-guided catalyst search uses GNN structure relaxation and adsorption-energy feedback; selected slabs are checked by DFT.

name: AtomAgents
demonstrated_target: metallic alloys, dislocations and fracture
boundary_conditions: explicit periodic boundaries; dislocation cells also have a free direction
evidence: Runs alloy property calculations, atomic relaxation and dislocation NEB; material-property experiments link simulation feedback to alloy hypotheses.

name: Adsorb-Agent
demonstrated_target: adsorbates on crystalline catalyst slabs
boundary_conditions: bulk-derived Miller-index slabs; explicit PBC not independently checked
evidence: LLM proposes adsorption sites and orientations, with relaxed atomistic adsorption-energy evaluation. Bulk IDs and slab Miller indices are documented.

name: LangSim
demonstrated_target: elemental crystals and Cu–Au solid solutions
boundary_conditions: crystal cells and energy–volume curves; explicit periodic-boundary flag not separately audited
locator: Individual project report §9 LangSim, especially crystal construction/optimization and bulk-modulus protocol
evidence: Project authors describe an LLM calling ASE/EMT or MACE workflows that construct a crystal, optimize its geometry, and evaluate energy versus volume to obtain the bulk modulus.
all_sources: https://arxiv.org/html/2411.15221v1 [Individual project report §9 LangSim, especially crystal construction/optimization and bulk-modulus protocol] | https://www.mpie.de/5063016/LangSim [Project description, Al bulk-modulus and Cu–Au inverse-design examples]
limitations: Date is the earliest dated primary report inspected here, not a verified software launch date; the official page identifies a 2024 hackathon. The later 34 Examples report is the same project and is not counted again.

name: MDCrow
demonstrated_target: proteins and common solvents
boundary_conditions: not resolved from inspected article; do not assume isolated molecules
evidence: Executes OpenMM MD and MDTraj analysis on protein tasks including temperature comparisons; demonstrated scope is biomolecular simulation.

name: MDAgent
demonstrated_target: LAMMPS materials thermodynamics
boundary_conditions: not resolved from inspected article
evidence: Generates, executes and reviews LAMMPS simulation code for material thermodynamic tasks.
limitations: Semi-automated: the paper explicitly retains human involvement. It is included because the scope includes LLM modification/execution, not only fully autonomous agents.

name: El Agente Q
demonstrated_target: organic molecules and coordination complexes
boundary_conditions: finite molecular calculations (ORCA/xTB)
locator: Abstract; corroborated by ChemGraph Discussion and Quntur Introduction
evidence: Quantum chemistry workflows include equilibrium geometries, vibrational/spectral and electronic-property calculations, with adaptive debugging.
all_sources: https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.02484 [Abstract; corroborated by ChemGraph Discussion and Quntur Introduction]

name: Aitomia
demonstrated_target: molecular spectra and reaction thermochemistry
boundary_conditions: finite molecular examples; no periodic demonstration coded
evidence: Demonstrated examples include hexanol IR and multi-species reaction enthalpy workflows using geometry optimization, frequency and electronic calculations.
limitations: The inspected preprint and current repository are distinct evidence versions. The current repository supports TS/IRC; no negative capability claim follows from uncoded tasks here.

name: MatAgent (Lv et al.)
demonstrated_target: water octamer, (H2O)8, total energy and maximum force
boundary_conditions: finite molecular cluster is the concrete worked target; PWDFT is a plane-wave engine, but boundary conditions for this cluster are not established by the article
evidence: GPT-4 chooses tools, supplies inputs and evaluates returned results. The structure tool supplies geometry and a PWDFT API executes first-principles energy/force calculations. The specific worked example asks for total energy and maximum force of a water octamer.
limitations: The article's materials terminology and Materials Project interface are broader than its concrete demonstrated water-cluster case. Do not label its physical target extended materials solely because it uses PWDFT; no MD mark is inferred from a general AIMD equation or cited PWDFT work. Distinct from other systems also called MatAgent.

name: ChemGraph
demonstrated_target: PubChem small molecules and reaction thermochemistry
boundary_conditions: finite molecular benchmarks; ASE supports PBC but support is not counted as a demonstration
evidence: Thirteen molecular tasks include DFT optimization, vibrations and reaction enthalpy/Gibbs calculations; no periodic benchmark is inferred from ASE support.

name: TopoMAS
demonstrated_target: SrSbO3 and Sr2Sb2O7 crystal generation; SrSbO3 topological classification
boundary_conditions: crystallographic space-group-constrained structures and VASP k-point files; periodic crystal workflow
evidence: LLM agents invoke CrystalFormer for crystal generation, plan and submit VASP calculations through an HPC API, inspect outputs, recover an intentionally corrupted completion check, and compute topological invariants with SymTopo.
limitations: Interactive human–AI framework; benchmark QA results do not determine simulation task marks. Journal and preprint are one system.

name: NAMD-Agent
demonstrated_target: proteins in explicit solvent and lipid membranes, including 1UBQ, 1L2Y and membrane-builder examples
boundary_conditions: Explicit periodic boundary conditions in the solution and membrane examples (SI §§6.1–6.6)
evidence: Gemini composes, executes and revises code to operate CHARMM-GUI, assemble solvated protein or membrane systems, run NAMD, and analyze actual 1 ns trajectories. Example simulation parameters explicitly enable periodic boundaries.
limitations: The inspected evidence is v1. T and D are positively coded; control over minimization settings alone is not used to infer a separate demonstrated O task. Protein or membrane boxes remain in the soft/biomolecular class despite PBC.

name: DREAMS
demonstrated_target: Sol27LC crystals and CO/Pt(111)
boundary_conditions: periodic crystal/lattice-constant and crystalline slab models
locator: Main text; Sol27LC and CO/Pt(111) challenges
evidence: Executes lattice-constant and adsorption-energy studies with DFT workflows and provenance checking.
all_sources: https://arxiv.org/html/2507.14267v2 [Main text; Sol27LC and CO/Pt(111) challenges]

name: SparksMatter
demonstrated_target: inorganic thermoelectrics, semiconductors and perovskite oxides
boundary_conditions: CIF crystal structures and periodic inorganic-material models; individual PBC flags not separately audited
evidence: A coder agent invokes MatterGen for structures and a MatterSim-based evaluation module for atomistic relaxation and formation-energy convex-hull construction. Case studies use this feedback for inorganic-material candidate design.
limitations: Included because actual atomistic force-field relaxation is executed, not because CGCNN predicts properties. Follow-up DFT and synthesis recommendations in the report are not counted as agent-executed DFT.

name: AutoSolvate-Agent
date_basis: dated original KDD workshop paper; exact first posting unresolved
demonstrated_target: water IR; molecular orbital, bond-order and charge analyses; benzaldehyde in implicit solvent; coordination complexes
boundary_conditions: finite molecular TeraChem calculations; PCM solvent in the benzaldehyde example
locator: Sections 4.1 Frequency Analysis and 4.2 Solvatochromism Prediction; Figures 2–3; Appendix A.2 Table 1
evidence: For water IR, the agent retrieves a geometry, interprets TeraChem's large-gradient frequency failure, inserts and completes a geometry optimization, and reruns frequency analysis. For benzaldehyde it sets up and executes PCM quantum chemistry and directs Multiwfn orbital-population analysis.
all_sources: https://openreview.net/pdf?id=ATEtqdGn6W [Sections 4.1 Frequency Analysis and 4.2 Solvatochromism Prediction; Figures 2–3; Appendix A.2 Table 1] | https://openreview.net/pdf/395d4c9eda83111a078ba05d86adcf84ec77e4aa.pdf [Appendix A.2, Table 1] | https://www.linkedin.com/in/fren5 [Author Fangning Ren's Publications entry for AutoSolvate-Agent]
limitations: The dated field uses 6 August 2025 printed on the original workshop paper. An author publication list gives 8 June; exact OpenReview first-posting time remains unresolved. Original PDF text was inspected via its index while direct OpenReview opening encountered a browser challenge. This LLM workflow is distinct from intent-based AutoSolvateWeb. Solvatochromism is qualitatively inferred from orbitals, not an excited-state dynamics calculation.

name: VASPilot
demonstrated_target: crystalline solids and transition-metal dichalcogenides
boundary_conditions: band structure/Brillouin-zone crystalline models
evidence: Demonstrates band structures, density of states, cutoff convergence, lattice-constant optimization and band-gap comparisons.

name: ChemAgents molecular simulation workflow
demonstrated_target: bridged azobenzenes and azobenzene ground-state conformers and IR/Raman spectra
boundary_conditions: molecular AIMD/DFT examples; gas and solvent spectral data; explicit simulation boundaries not independently audited
locator: Abstract; Figure 1; Results and discussion / Computation–experimentation integration and automated workflow execution; Conclusions
evidence: LLM agents formulate the study plan and coordinate automated computations. The Computation Performer runs ground-state AIMD conformer sampling and DFT IR/Raman calculations; the paper explicitly separates these from human-designed and trained neural-network analysis.
all_sources: https://pubs.rsc.org/en/content/articlehtml/2026/sc/d5sc08794e [Abstract; Figure 1; Results and discussion / Computation–experimentation integration and automated workflow execution; Conclusions] | https://doi.org/10.26434/chemrxiv-2025-4kh1r [Version 1 record, 12 August 2025; abstract]
limitations: The system's molecular-computation demonstration is counted once, rather than counting the accompanying robotic experiment or spectral prediction model as additional systems. Ground-state sampling and steady-state spectra do not demonstrate nonadiabatic photoisomerization dynamics or validated transition-state/IRC searches. Earlier ChemAgents platform work may establish an earlier family release, but this is the first verified atomistic demonstration located in this screening.

name: AMLP
demonstrated_target: acridine molecular-crystal polymorphs
boundary_conditions: monoclinic crystal cells, cell optimization and crystal AIMD; molecular identity does not make the demonstrated crystal an isolated molecule
evidence: LLM agents assist electronic-structure code and parameter selection, input construction and conversion in a pipeline that performs DFT geometry/cell optimization and AIMD, trains a MACE potential and validates it with relaxation and NVE/NVT dynamics on acridine crystals.
limitations: LLM assistance sits within a substantially scripted pipeline. Article revisions and the JCTC counterpart are one system. MLIP development itself is not a new seventh task code.

name: ToPolyAgent
demonstrated_target: coarse-grained bead-spring linear, ring, brush, star and dendrimer polymers with solvent
boundary_conditions: Polymer–solvent simulation boxes are explicit; PBC is not separately resolved from the inspected article
evidence: LLM agents invoke polymer/solvent construction and LAMMPS simulation tools. Brush and star examples execute dynamics, and interactive feedback changes grafting density or extends a simulation; research examples compare solvent interactions and polymer conformation.
all_sources: https://arxiv.org/html/2510.12091v1 [§§II.1–II.3; Results §§III.1–III.3; Figs.2–3] | https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.12091 [Primary arXiv record and submission history]
limitations: Coarse-grained rather than all-atom MD. Interactive and autonomous modes are both included. The article HTML has a later rendering timestamp despite retaining the v1 identifier; date uses the primary submission record. Conformational/transport observables are coded under D, not F.

name: GENIUS
demonstrated_target: MC2D/MC3D materials; PdS2 geometry-relaxation example
boundary_conditions: 2D/3D crystal database targets; PdS2 example has a 7×7×2 k-point mesh
locator: Prompt Dataset; Automated Error Handling; Results/Figs.6–7
evidence: LLMs generate Quantum ESPRESSO input and repair failed executions using a parameter knowledge graph. The benchmark contains structural relaxation and single-shot DFT tasks; the worked PdS2 case generates BFGS relaxation input and shows an execution/recovery timeline.
all_sources: https://arxiv.org/html/2512.06404v1 [Prompt Dataset; Automated Error Handling; Results/Figs.6–7] | https://www.nature.com/articles/s43246-026-01167-0 [Journal abstract]
limitations: Task marks denote executed calculation types, not scientific completion. The preprint's run-to-completion wording must not overwrite the journal's early-execution-validation qualification. Geometry retrieval/standardization alone was not assigned an additional construction mark.

name: LAMMPS-Agents
demonstrated_target: elemental metals and binary alloys, including gold and Cu–Au
boundary_conditions: crystal models; exact PBC flags not independently audited from the inspected repository
locator: README; lammps_agents.py demonstration prompts and simulation workflow
evidence: Official project implements a natural-language multi-agent simulator with specialized structure, potential, property, HPC and analysis agents.
all_sources: https://github.com/ANL-NST/LAMMPS-Agents [README; lammps_agents.py demonstration prompts and simulation workflow] | https://doi.org/10.1039/D5DD00435G [Introduction; Results static/dynamic property examples; Conclusion] | https://www.alcf.anl.gov/publications/multi-agentic-ai-framework-end-end-atomistic-simulations [Publication metadata]
limitations: The publisher's full text was available as a cached primary search response but direct opens returned 403; official repository and source were also inspected. Distinct from both DynaMate systems, AtomAgents and URSA. No soft-matter mark is inferred from future extensibility.

name: DynaMate (protein–ligand)
demonstrated_target: proteins and protein–ligand complexes, including BRD4 BD1 inhibitor MD and endpoint binding energies
boundary_conditions: Periodic boundary conditions with explicit TIP3P solvent and neutralizing ions (§4.3)
evidence: Planner/worker/analyzer agents build and parameterize solvated protein complexes, minimize geometry, execute GROMACS equilibration/production, and repair failed tool calls. BRD4 examples run 100 ns dynamics followed by MM/PBSA binding-energy analysis.
all_sources: https://arxiv.org/html/2512.10034v1 [§§2.1–2.5; §§4.2–4.4; SI Appendix B] | https://openreview.net/pdf?id=NkLAjIzwei [Title, author list and abstract of SimBioChem 2025 workshop counterpart]
limitations: The dated field uses the verified arXiv date; an earlier DynAgent workshop version is identified but its posting date is unresolved, so this is not a secure earliest-appearance claim. This is unrelated to the LAMMPS/Moltemplate DynaMate of de Gillis et al. Endpoint MM/PBSA analysis is included under D, without E/F marks.

name: AGAPI-Agents
demonstrated_target: TiAu relaxation, Al substitution in GaN, semiconductor defects and interfaces
boundary_conditions: POSCAR crystal cells, supercells and heterostructures; explicit PBC flag not separately audited
locator: §2.4 ML Force Field Optimization; §2.5 Case Study1/Fig.8
evidence: The agent runs ALIGNN-FF iterative relaxation for an arbitrary TiAu structure. Its semiconductor-defect workflow constructs a supercell, substitutes atoms, optimizes the same structure and calculates a tight-binding band structure.
all_sources: https://arxiv.org/html/2512.11935v1 [§2.4 ML Force Field Optimization; §2.5 Case Study1/Fig.8]
limitations: Database retrieval and scalar predictor calls alone are not the inclusion basis. No MD or protein-simulation mark is inferred from the platform's tool list. Journal and preprint count once.

name: MASTER
demonstrated_target: CO on Cu(100) adatoms and M–N–C catalysts
boundary_conditions: explicit 4×4 periodic six-layer Cu(100) slab
locator: Computational methods; Fig.2; Supplementary geometry tips
evidence: LLM reasoning chooses catalyst candidates and executes atomistic adsorption-energy simulations; Cu(100) geometry is explicitly periodic.
all_sources: https://arxiv.org/html/2512.13930v1 [Computational methods; Fig.2; Supplementary geometry tips]

name: VASP Agent
demonstrated_target: bulk crystals, CO adsorption slabs, methane activation and acetylene hydrogenation on Pd/Ag
boundary_conditions: VASP periodic bulk and surface cells; surface k-point meshes explicitly reported
evidence: A separately proposed domain agent plans and executes VASP structural relaxation, band-structure and adsorption calculations, plus surface-reaction CI-NEB. The paper evaluates completion separately from physical accuracy and reports persistent TS accuracy failures.
limitations: Do not deduplicate with VASPilot or AutoDFT. Isolated CO is a reference component of the adsorption workflow, not a demonstrated separate molecular research domain. R denotes executed NEB task coverage and does not establish full mechanism validation.

name: Masgent
demonstrated_target: LaCoO3 vacancies and metallic/crystalline materials
boundary_conditions: crystal/supercell/slab models documented
evidence: Agent executes LaCoO3 vacancy construction and MLP defect-energy workflow. VASP workflows are prepared; the agent does not directly execute VASP.
limitations: Do not equate VASP input preparation with completed VASP calculations; task marks refer to demonstrated MLP/structure work.

name: CASCADE
date_basis: verified CASCADE-title arXiv date; predecessor posting date unresolved
demonstrated_target: Li_xCoO2 battery cathode crystals and MLIP density/volume comparisons
boundary_conditions: crystalline materials; explicit PBC wording not separately audited
locator: Section 2.3, Collaborative research with memory; Fig. 5; Appendix B.3
evidence: In human-agent exchanges, the system selects MLIPs, executes structural relaxations and energy calculations, and obtains lithium-intercalation voltages. Separate wet-lab and database-only cases do not determine inclusion.
all_sources: https://arxiv.org/html/2512.23880v1 [Section 2.3, Collaborative research with memory; Fig. 5; Appendix B.3]
limitations: Only the inspected crystalline simulation case determines the target class and task marks. Molecular QC questions listed in SciSkillBench are not by themselves treated as demonstrated additional targets. Human guidance is retained. SkillPuzzler is a related earlier title, not counted again. The earlier SkillPuzzler workshop predecessor predates 29 December; this dated field identifies the verified CASCADE-title preprint, not a secure family-first appearance.

name: CatMaster
demonstrated_target: Fe(110)/CO, Au(111)/O paths, catalytic surface models and single-atom catalysts
boundary_conditions: bulk/slab/adsorbate models; exact PBC settings not separately audited
locator: Results/Operational autonomy; Literature-grounded model construction; Mechanistic autonomy; Full-cycle SAC design
evidence: CatMaster plans and executes adsorption screening, DOS workflows, catalytic model construction and a MACE-driven Au(111)-O TS/NEB task with vibrational analysis. The paper explicitly discusses a run that analyzed the endpoint minimum instead of the TS.
all_sources: https://arxiv.org/html/2601.13508v3 [Results/Operational autonomy; Literature-grounded model construction; Mechanistic autonomy; Full-cycle SAC design]
limitations: Inspected v3 is from May2026; first report was January2026. R/F are positive task coverage, not an assertion all runs satisfy scientific acceptance. MatBench scalar-prediction exercises are not the atomistic inclusion basis.

name: QUASAR
demonstrated_target: bulk Cu/NiO/Al and porous crystals, plus liquid-water NPT equilibration
boundary_conditions: periodic electronic-structure crystals, MOF/COF adsorption cells and condensed water; exact water PBC flags not separately audited
evidence: Strategist, Operator and Evaluator agents execute QE convergence/relaxation and NiO electronic calculations, prepare doped perovskites, run liquid-water NPT and Al melting MD, and execute porous-framework adsorption Monte Carlo.
limitations: Cross-domain follows a separately demonstrated liquid-water task and extended-material tasks; it is not inferred from an ASE interface. Monte Carlo adsorption does not receive D by itself; water and Al MD provide that evidence. AI4X and arXiv reports are one system.

name: El Agente Estructural
demonstrated_target: molecules, organometallic complexes and TS-like geometries
boundary_conditions: finite molecular cases; slabs/solids are future extensions in inspected v1
evidence: Invokes xTB constrained optimization to create intended molecular geometry; agentic geometric operations are real. Subsequent independent DFT TS checks are not coded as agent TS execution.
limitations: Included despite editor emphasis because xTB constrained relaxation is an actual quantum-chemical computation, beyond pure string/generative molecular design.

name: El Agente Quntur
demonstrated_target: molecular and coordination quantum chemistry
boundary_conditions: finite molecular cases including isocyanide and acetylacetone
locator: Results/case studies; Discussion/Geometric reasoning; Appendix B
evidence: Demonstrates electronic methods, optimization/frequencies and reaction-path cases; isocyanide mechanistic refinement includes TS correction. NEB geometry failures are discussed, so this is task coverage rather than blanket success.
all_sources: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.04850v3 [Results/case studies; Discussion/Geometric reasoning; Appendix B]

name: El Agente Gráfico
demonstrated_target: finite-molecule quantum chemistry and explicit microsolvation ensembles; metal-organic frameworks
boundary_conditions: finite molecular gas/implicit-solvent/15-water-cluster examples; separate MOF crystal/CIF construction and MLIP relaxation
locator: Sections 2.1–2.3; Figure 3; Appendix C; Appendix D.1.7
evidence: An LLM routing agent orchestrates typed single-point, optimization, frequency and TDDFT nodes. Molecular examples generate CREST conformers and a 15-water microsolvation cluster, optimize them, check imaginary modes and calculate ensemble spectra. A separate demonstrated MOF workflow constructs CIF structures, relaxes them with MACE and analyzes porosity.
all_sources: https://arxiv.org/html/2602.17902v1 [Sections 2.1–2.3; Figure 3; Appendix C; Appendix D.1.7] | https://arxiv.org/html/2602.17902v2 [Version 2 front matter, abstract, Sections 2.1–2.3 and Appendix E]
limitations: Same research family as Q/Quntur/Estructural but a separately described execution-graph system, so not deduplicated merely by family. Cross-domain classification reflects actual finite molecular and MOF demonstrations. Its molecular imaginary-frequency failure recovery is not evidence of TS/IRC execution. The present matrix retains the inspected v1 task basis. Version 2 (7 August) has a revised title/author list and reports disulfide redox-mechanism work; the blank R cell is not a claim that the current system has no mechanistic applications. The polishing manuscript cites v2.

name: El Agente Sólido
demonstrated_target: crystals, Pt(111) oxygenated adsorbates, NMC-811, MOFs/COFs
boundary_conditions: Quantum ESPRESSO solid-state k-point workflows and periodic SQS/framework cells
evidence: A separate solid-state agent team runs QE and UMA relaxation/property workflows, constructs adsorbates/SQS and reticular structures, and uses Phonopy for Si/NaCl/Fe phonon bands and temperature-dependent thermal quantities.
limitations: Separate architecture/tool composition and benchmark from Q, Quntur, Estructural and Forjador, with family-level merge available. OER free-energy diagrams are not a transition-path/TS search, so no R is assigned from them.

name: Catalyst-Agent
demonstrated_target: catalyst slabs/adsorbates screened for ORR, NRR and CO2RR
boundary_conditions: crystalline bulk-derived slab construction; explicit PBC flags not separately audited
evidence: The LLM retrieves crystals, modifies surfaces and invokes FAIRchem AdsorbML/UMA to place adsorbates, relax geometries and calculate adsorption energies, then revises near-miss candidates using returned energetic feedback.
all_sources: https://arxiv.org/html/2603.01311v1 [§2.1.4–2.1.6; Energy Evaluation Server; reaction-screening results]
limitations: DFT validation is downstream future confirmation in the inspected report, not counted as agent-executed DFT. Reaction labels do not imply explicit TS or path search.

name: TritonDFT
demonstrated_target: DFTBench crystalline materials spanning metals, insulators and correlated/topological solids
boundary_conditions: periodic QE crystals and Brillouin-zone sampling; 73-material benchmark
evidence: A Plan–Execute–Refine agent runs QE variable-cell relaxation, SCF, band-gap and DOS calculations; its phonon case autonomously sequences pw.x, ph.x, q2r.x and matdyn.x.
limitations: A software-supported task list is not used to add unsupported task marks. Broadening beyond the inspected four main tasks and phonon case would require further evidence.

name: Chelatron
date_basis: dated official DOE/LANL project presentation, not paper publication date
demonstrated_target: actinium–chelator coordination complexes
boundary_conditions: finite Architector metal–ligand complexes evaluated by high-throughput quantum calculations
locator: LANL contribution, slide headed CHELATRON: AI-Driven Molecular Discovery for Cancer Treatment (printed slide 76)
evidence: The LANL project report describes Nemotron-generated chemical hypotheses, GenMol candidate generation, Architector complex construction and high-throughput quantum binding-affinity evaluation, with those assessments returned to the LLM for iterative hypothesis refinement.
all_sources: https://science.osti.gov/-/media/About/pdf/scac/meetings/2026/lab-contributions-to-GM-03-24-2026v2.pdf [LANL contribution, slide headed CHELATRON: AI-Driven Molecular Discovery for Cancer Treatment (printed slide 76)]
limitations: Evidence is an official DOE/LANL project presentation rather than the original ChemRxiv paper, whose identifier was not resolved. The meeting document is dated 24 March 2026; the later perspective instead lists the preprint on 31 July 2026. This earlier public project appearance and the later paper should be deduplicated, not counted twice. xTB optimization details reported by secondary paper listings are not used to code O here.

name: MatSciAgent
demonstrated_target: Al and NiAl crystal MD; auxiliary continuum tasks
boundary_conditions: FCC and CIF-derived crystalline models; explicit PBC not independently audited
locator: Molecular dynamics Case 1; Joint Implementation; Figs.11–12
evidence: Executes Al NVE MD and CIF-generated NiAl NVT MD; continuum-only examples do not determine inclusion.

name: OpenClaw computational-chemistry skills workflow
demonstrated_target: isolated methane/oxygen preparation and quantum-chemical optimization; reactive molecular methane/oxygen mixture
boundary_conditions: isolated CH4/O2 QC followed by a packed 50-CH4/100-O2 molecular gas mixture; MD boundary conditions not independently resolved
family: OpenClaw computational chemistry / Ding et al.
locator: Section 3 Case Study: Methane Oxidation Reactive MD Automation; Figure 3
evidence: From a natural-language request, the LLM-controlled workflow builds isolated molecules, runs B3LYP geometry optimizations, packs a methane/oxygen system, performs 3000-K reactive Deep-Potential/LAMMPS MD and extracts reactions with ReacNetGenerator. Repeated end-to-end demonstrations use error feedback to repair stages.
all_sources: https://arxiv.org/html/2603.25522v1 [Section 3 Case Study: Methane Oxidation Reactive MD Automation; Figure 3]
limitations: This record counts the separately reported chemistry skills/workflow, not every use of the general OpenClaw host. Periodic-box use would not make the simulated molecular gas an extended solid. Reaction-network extraction from reactive MD is not coded as a saddle/IRC path-search demonstration. The Deep Potential is supplied pretrained, not developed by the agent.

name: Protomia
demonstrated_target: Diels–Alder reaction energy and molecular thermochemistry
boundary_conditions: finite molecular reaction examples; platform's broader supported periodic scope is not inferred as demonstrated
locator: Usage Examples / Reaction Energy and Thermodynamics; worked-session screenshot
evidence: The official worked example shows autonomous reaction calculations and an output spreadsheet of extracted species and reaction energies. The page distinguishes this from its list of generally supported calculation types.

Evidence is developer documentation and a developer-authored perspective demonstration; no independent paper evaluation was located. TS/IRC/MD appear in supported-feature lists but are left uncoded without a verified worked demonstration. First-release date is developer-reported.

name: SimMOF
demonstrated_target: UiO-66/CO2 transport, HKUST-1 and ZIF-8 binding, high-throughput MOF adsorption

For HKUST-1/ZIF-8 it generates adsorption configurations, prescreens with MACE and executes host/guest optimization, DFT binding-energy and charge-density/Bader workflows.
limitations: Inspected latest v3 is August2026, with March first appearance. Mention of vibrational frequencies as a generic scheduling example was not assigned an F mark. Human confirmation in the shown corrected MD case is retained.

name: PolyJarvis
demonstrated_target: amorphous homopolymers
boundary_conditions: condensed simulation cells; self-imaging/PPPM documented; PBC wording not separately resolved
evidence: Builds polymer cells and orchestrates equilibration, cooling, density, glass-transition and mechanical-property MD workflows.

name: FermiLink
demonstrated_target: finite molecular electronic structure and biomolecular/soft-matter MD; additional materials simulations
boundary_conditions: multiple packages and models; no single boundary condition assigned
locator: Sections II.1–II.2; Table S1 Chemistry and Molecular Science (GROMACS, LAMMPS, Psi4, PySCF); Table S2 CP2K
evidence: Codex-driven workflows rerun molecular electronic-structure and molecular-dynamics packages. The paper distinguishes newly executed simulations from merely replotted figures; only executed cases support these marks.
all_sources: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.03460v1 [Sections II.1–II.2; Table S1 Chemistry and Molecular Science (GROMACS, LAMMPS, Psi4, PySCF); Table S2 CP2K]
limitations: General scientific infrastructure; non-atomistic physics and engineering tasks are not counted as chemistry evidence. Replotted and blocked tasks are not simulation successes. T/O/F/R remain unencoded without case-level evidence in this pass.

name: MatClaw
demonstrated_target: monolayer CuInP2S6 ferroelectric MD, potential distillation and domain-wall dynamics
boundary_conditions: 2D material and MD supercell targets; explicit PBC flags not separately audited
evidence: The code-writing LLM runs active-learning force-field distillation, atomistic energy/force evaluation, Curie-temperature MD and a field/temperature search for domain-wall propagation. Demonstrations discuss failed sampling/equilibration choices and researcher interventions.
all_sources: https://arxiv.org/html/2604.02688v1 [§3.1–3.3 Demonstration tasks and failure analysis]
limitations: Guided autonomy: high-level expert constraints and literature self-learning assist the agent. Do not count the March2026 APS presentation on the same CuInP2S6 agent as a second system; exact identity of that early abstract is retained in screening.

name: El Agente Forjador
demonstrated_target: molecular QC plus quantum dynamics
boundary_conditions: finite molecular examples; quantum-state dynamics does not imply periodic materials
evidence: Creates and reuses tools for molecular optimization, frequencies/thermochemistry and excited states; hybrid cases couple electronic structure to quantum dynamics.
limitations: D is quantum dynamics, not necessarily atomistic MD. The physical target is coded by demonstrated molecular calculations, not software breadth.

name: MDAgent (biomolecular, 2026)
demonstrated_target: soluble and membrane proteins, protein–DNA/ligand systems and TMEM16F/XKR8 scramblase dynamics
boundary_conditions: Three-dimensional PBC for all simulated systems; explicit aqueous or lipid environments (Methods §4.5)
evidence: The LLM multi-agent system connects research planning to GROMACS system construction, steepest-descent minimization, equilibration and production. Demonstrations include membrane-protein dynamics and enhanced sampling; methods specify 3D periodic systems.
all_sources: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2604.18622 [Results §§2.1–2.4; Methods §4.5, PDF pp.43–46] | https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.18622 [Primary record, title/authors and first submission]
limitations: Distinct from the 2025 materials LAMMPS MDAgent. Umbrella-sampling PMF, metadynamics and SMD transport analyses remain D; no E/F/R mark is inferred from statistical free energies or transport paths. Some evaluation dimensions concern plans/reports, so task coding relies on the separately described executed simulation cases, not review scores.

name: VirtualLab_CC
demonstrated_target: stabilized Criegee intermediates and biogenic terpenes; molecular conformers, thermochemistry and PES study
boundary_conditions: finite molecular Gaussian/ORCA calculations with CREST/xTB conformer search
locator: Section 2.1 and Table 1; prototype Criegee case study; Section 5.3; Section 6 Limitations
evidence: Claude coordinates method proposals, task decomposition and failure interpretation around executed CREST conformer, DFT optimization/frequency and coupled-cluster jobs. The molecular campaign includes real production outputs and automatic repair of cluster-invocation failures, with human approvals for scientific decisions.
all_sources: https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S2949747726000230 [Section 2.1 and Table 1; prototype Criegee case study; Section 5.3; Section 6 Limitations] | https://github.com/CCBG-Lab/VirtualLab_CC [README / Architecture; HPC Integration; Method Protocols; release v1.1.0] | https://doi.org/10.26434/chemrxiv.15002407/v1 [Original preprint record, 27 April 2026]
limitations: The paper explicitly says transition-state location remains semi-manual and no automated reaction-discovery engine is included. Path/TS task R is therefore conservatively left uncoded here. Human approval at critical scientific decisions does not exclude demonstrated LLM planning, invocation and repair. Journal text was inspected through the indexed publisher original; direct opening returned HTTP 403.

name: XDFT
demonstrated_target: correlated and structurally complex crystalline metal/semiconductor mismatches
boundary_conditions: VASP crystal/supercell calculations with k-point density; defect, strain and polymorph interventions
locator: Architecture pp.2–3; Methods p.10, Hypothesis library/First-principles/Bayesian hypothesis selection
evidence: For each material an LLM advisor contributes a per-material hypothesis score to a Bayesian selector. The selected intervention modifies crystal structures or VASP inputs and executes first-principles tests; the resulting verdict updates the selector's state.
all_sources: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2604.26703v1 [Architecture pp.2–3; Methods p.10, Hypothesis library/First-principles/Bayesian hypothesis selection]
limitations: The LLM is not the entire selector: v1 explicitly weights the advisor score 0.2. Include because the LLM influences actual per-material computational choices. Later revisions change the benchmark and title; do not mix their result counts. R is chemical/structural paths, not diagnostic mechanism attribution, so none is assigned.

name: TSAgent
demonstrated_target: heterogeneous catalytic reactions on slabs
boundary_conditions: VASP slab geometry; 2×2×1 k-point grid explicitly reported
evidence: Adapts geometry optimization, NEB and vibrational TS verification on OC20NEB surface-reaction cases.

name: Lang2MLIP
demonstrated_target: graphite/Li2CO3/LEDC/liquid-electrolyte multilayer solid-electrolyte interphase
boundary_conditions: solid, amorphous and liquid component cells and interfaces; explicit PBC flags not separately audited
evidence: Agents construct 60 component/interface configurations and an LLM decision-maker adaptively chooses reference calculations, MD sampling, training and evaluation. The demonstrated reference is the PFP interatomic potential, not DFT.
limitations: Target coding follows the integrated solid–electrolyte interface study. Generic support for polymers, isolated clusters and other structure classes does not establish separate demonstrated research domains. No DFT-execution claim is inferred from interchangeable reference backends.

name: AtomisticSkills
demonstrated_target: solid electrolytes, MOFs, catalyst surfaces and protein–ligand complexes
boundary_conditions: crystal and surface cells plus explicit-water biomolecular MD; not a single PBC class
evidence: Coding agents construct and relax solids, submit DFT energies/forces, sample configurations by MD, and execute explicit-water MD refinement of docked protein–ligand complexes.
limitations: A skills/tool harness for general coding agents. Human review of campaign plans is retained. Drug docking alone does not establish inclusion; the executed downstream MD does. MD-derived binding free energies are under D, not vibrational F.

name: ChatMOSP
demonstrated_target: Pd and Pt catalytic nanoparticles under CO oxidation
boundary_conditions: finite metal nanoparticles with exposed surface facets; finite nanoparticles remain material/surface targets, not isolated molecular chemistry
locator: pp.5–12, workflow and Pd/Pt morphology-reconstruction case studies
evidence: An OpenClaw/GLM-5 agent translates reaction conditions, obtains model parameters and executes MOSP multiscale atomistic morphology reconstruction plus kinetic Monte Carlo. Pd temperature-series structures and Pt pressure/coverage/morphology/activity studies are demonstrated.
all_sources: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2605.24265 [pp.5–12, workflow and Pd/Pt morphology-reconstruction case studies]
limitations: Its actual physics simulation is sufficient for inclusion although the six-bin scheme only encodes structure reconstruction. KMC does not receive the MD/quantum-dynamics code D, and a prescribed kinetic network does not establish TS/path search R. Energetic parameters are retrieved, not newly calculated by the agent.

name: AutoDFT
demonstrated_target: bulk/surface materials plus standalone CO and H2O optimization/vibration tasks
boundary_conditions: VASP crystal/slab workflows and finite molecular targets represented in plane-wave cells; molecular target identity is distinct from cell periodicity
evidence: A seven-agent VASP framework performs adaptive planning, monitoring and recovery. Its evaluated 34-task table explicitly includes ionic/volume relaxation, SCF/DOS, DFPT phonons and MD, including standalone CO/H2O relaxation and vibration cases alongside crystal and slab tasks.
limitations: Cross-domain is based on evaluated standalone molecular tasks, not VASP's general support. The system is separately proposed from its VASPBench benchmark and therefore one system, not one system per calculation type. Gaussian portability is an aspiration, not demonstrated evidence.

name: MLIPilot
demonstrated_target: QM7 molecular systems and periodic Cu supercells
boundary_conditions: article explicitly contrasts finite molecular QM7 and periodic Cu EMT datasets
evidence: LLMs edit MACE training code and submit experiments whose fixed atomistic evaluation executes energy/force tests, FIRE geometry relaxation and 5,000-step NVE dynamics. Agents accept or revert experiments using returned physical diagnostics on molecular and Cu benchmarks.
limitations: The LLM optimizes training rather than directly writing each MD step, but actual simulation feedback determines its choices. Pre-generated QM7 B3LYP labels are not counted as agent-run DFT. Source calls this MLIPilot, distinct from VASPilot.

name: CatDT
demonstrated_target: working heterogeneous catalyst surfaces
boundary_conditions: slab/bulk/facet construction with gas–solid and liquid–solid models
evidence: Builds catalyst surfaces, proposes mechanisms, searches paths/TS and computes kinetics using atomistic tools; liquid–solid capability is not finite-molecule evidence.

name: Paimon
demonstrated_target: LiPF6 liquid electrolytes in DEC/DMC/PC and crystalline solid-electrolyte ion diffusion
boundary_conditions: Liquid cells explicitly require PBC in all three directions (§3.6); crystalline solid-electrolyte MD is separately demonstrated
locator: §§2.1, 2.4–2.5; Fig.4 actual MD runs; Fig.5 solid-electrolyte example; Methods §§3.5–3.6
evidence: Orchestrator/executor agents build electrolyte cells with PACKMOL, relax structures, run LAMMPS equilibration and production, and revise workflows using intermediate feedback. The article distinguishes 30 actual liquid-MD runs from gated tests with precomputed outputs, and separately demonstrates a crystalline solid-electrolyte MD workflow using LLaMP.
all_sources: https://arxiv.org/html/2606.09422v1 [§§2.1, 2.4–2.5; Fig.4 actual MD runs; Fig.5 solid-electrolyte example; Methods §§3.5–3.6]
limitations: Cross-domain coding follows demonstrated liquid and solid examples, not general software support. Many repeated evaluations replace expensive dynamics with precomputed outputs; actual MD evidence is explicitly limited to the separate full runs and worked example. Transport coefficients are D, not F or electronic E.

name: MDForge
demonstrated_target: SAMPL host–guest binding free energies
boundary_conditions: not resolved from inspected article; explicit/implicit solvent workflow details need separate audit
evidence: LLM writes and refines MD pipelines with physics feedback on host–guest binding benchmarks.

name: URSA LAMMPS agent
demonstrated_target: metal crystals/liquids, Cu cohesive energy and thermomechanical properties
boundary_conditions: bulk crystal/liquid atomistic models and stacking-fault cells; exact PBC flags not separately audited
evidence: The LLM selects a potential from NIST metadata, authors and runs LAMMPS input, iteratively repairs execution failures, and hands outputs to analysis agents. Benchmarks include cohesive energies, volume curves, thermal expansion, liquid RDF, melting and generalized stacking-fault energy.
limitations: First date follows source metadata, even though the arXiv identifier begins 2607. Distinct from LAMMPS-Agents (Vriza) and the generic URSA framework. No R mark is assigned to static generalized stacking-fault energies without an explicit path search.

name: AdsMind
demonstrated_target: adsorbate configurations on catalyst slabs
boundary_conditions: cell and periodic boundary conditions explicitly retained in ASE slab reconstruction
evidence: Closed-loop agent uses MLFF relaxation feedback to revise adsorption hypotheses. Main benchmark has Langevin warmup disabled; no MD mark is assigned.

name: LADeQ
demonstrated_target: alkanes C15H32/C20H42, coronene and porphyrin electronic correlation energies
boundary_conditions: finite molecular PySCF CCSD/CISD; STO-3G and single-thread evaluation
evidence: The LLM proposes approximations, edits PySCF CCSD/CISD implementations, and revises them using computed correlation-energy errors, timing and diagnostic logs. The paper reports executed molecular calculations for development and cross-molecule evaluation.
limitations: An algorithm-discovery workflow rather than a general researcher-facing QC assistant. Inclusion follows the explicit rule allowing LLM code modification and feedback decisions in executed molecular electronic-structure calculations. Demonstrated conclusions are limited to ground-state correlation energies, four molecules and a minimal basis; no geometry, path or dynamics capabilities are inferred.

name: Agent-MD
demonstrated_target: montmorillonite clay–water desorption
boundary_conditions: explicit periodic boundaries in all three directions
evidence: LLM reasoning supports campaign construction and event review around deterministic GCMC–MD; production cycles need no live LLM invocation.
limitations: Selective LLM placement is included; counting requires actual planning/modification decisions, not a live LLM at every MD step.

name: CGMas
demonstrated_target: homopolymers and copolymers modeled with paired all-atom and coarse-grained force fields
boundary_conditions: Explicit cubic periodic cells and PBC in x, y and z (Methods §4.3)
evidence: LLM topology and mapping agents coordinate construction, review and self-correction. Tools build periodic polymer cells, minimize close contacts, execute atomistic annealing/equilibration, derive coarse-grained potentials from the trajectory, and run CG dynamics. PAN and autonomous polymer cases provide executed workflow evidence.
all_sources: https://arxiv.org/html/2608.06694v1 [§§2.1–2.4; PAN worked example, Fig.2; Methods §§4.2–4.5]
limitations: Human checkpoints are retained in the interactive route. Numerical stages use deterministic tools under LLM orchestration. Density, cooling-scan glass transitions and Boltzmann-inverted potentials do not establish vibrational thermochemistry; F remains blank.

name: Evolving TS workflows
demonstrated_target: TS1X molecular elementary reactions
boundary_conditions: finite molecular endpoint/TS geometries
evidence: LLM evolves TS-search code; execution feedback includes Hessian and IRC endpoint checks. The LLM optimizes the workflow rather than directly making every reaction decision.

name: ARCHE
demonstrated_target: organic/organometallic molecular mechanisms
boundary_conditions: finite molecular asymmetric, radical and Ni-catalysis examples
locator: Abstract; SI TSPipeline/C.10 independently checked by parent researcher
evidence: Closed-loop mechanistic hypotheses are checked computationally across stereocontrol, radical cleavage and Ni-catalyzed selectivity examples.
all_sources: https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.11147 [Abstract; SI TSPipeline/C.10 independently checked by parent researcher]
limitations: Full PDF exceeds web-reader size limit; main inclusion/object/task claims use the abstract. Parent independently inspected SI mapping/force-field/TS and frequency/IRC/endpoint chain. Do not infer absent geometric or scientific validation capabilities.

name: Multireference QC agent
demonstrated_target: QUEST molecular excited states and transition-metal complexes
boundary_conditions: finite molecular ORCA calculations
evidence: Selects active spaces, submits ORCA calculations, recovers convergence and identifies electronic states; evaluation covers molecular vertical transition energies.

name: SQD-Agent
demonstrated_target: small-molecule ground-state energies including N2 and CH2O
boundary_conditions: finite molecular electronic Hamiltonians
locator: Section I Figs. 1–5; Section II Discussions and Future Scope
evidence: An LLM orchestration layer generates and executes molecular SQD electronic-structure workflows on classical simulators and a quantum processor, with explicit human confirmation before hardware submission.
all_sources: https://arxiv.org/html/2609.39302v1 [Section I Figs. 1–5; Section II Discussions and Future Scope]
limitations: Proof of concept in a minimal basis; the authors explicitly describe human-supervised reconfiguration and no autonomous closed feedback loop. Inclusion does not imply full autonomy or quantum advantage.

name: MLP Copilot
demonstrated_target: bare and oxide-shell aluminum nanoparticle oxidation
boundary_conditions: finite nanoparticles in a reactive simulation environment; atomistic materials target regardless of box periodicity
locator: §1.1; Methods §3.3 Human-Audited Multiagent Framework; MovieS1 description
evidence: Language-model agents organize evidence, assist validation planning and prepare decisions in an executed active-learning MLP campaign, including CP2K energy/force labeling, model evaluation and ANP oxidation MD. Scientific acceptance and deployment remain human controlled.
all_sources: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13684298/ [§1.1; Methods §3.3 Human-Audited Multiagent Framework; MovieS1 description] | https://github.com/flarecentury/mlpcopilot [README/Simulation Data And DigAuto; Start With Initial Data]
limitations: Human-audited planning/validation assistance qualifies under the broad inclusion rule; do not describe it as an autonomous MD scientist or claim the LLM directly made every execution decision. October15 is the inspected online publication date, not a verified first software release. Auto-MLP and the current runtime are treated as one campaign family to avoid duplicate counting.

name: Magnolia
demonstrated_target: aromatic molecules, gas-phase butane and modified DNA
boundary_conditions: finite molecular QC/gas-phase dynamics and solvated DNA cells
evidence: The agent generates and optimizes aromatic structures, evaluates electronic properties, runs butane dynamics and a relaxed torsion scan, and constructs and tracks modified-DNA MD campaigns.
limitations: Human-reviewed memory and scientific decisions remain explicit. A torsional scan is not coded as a TS/IRC proof. Docking claims and proprietary targets do not determine task marks.
